## Installing git

Before you start, check whether you already have git:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Request the path to your git.exe
which git

# Request the version of your git installation
git --version
```

if the return is something like the message below you need to install it. 
```{r}
#| eval: false
git: command not found
```

----

Mac users may be prompted help immediately and they should accept. 


If you are not offered to have it installed for you, install it manually: 

- visit [https://git-scm.com/install/](https://git-scm.com/install/) 
- find the right version for your local machine (Mac, Linux)


On **Linux**
```{r}
#| eval: false
sudo apt-add-repository ppa:git-core/ppa
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install git


# keep it up to date
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install git
```

On **Mac** via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/)
```{r}
#| eval: false
brew install git

# keep it up to date
brew update && brew upgrade git
```

On **Windows**, install [gitforwindows](https://gitforwindows.org/).
It comes with the Git bash which gives access to the Bash shell in addition to git.
If you already have git installed, it may be good to update it (via shell/git command line)

```{r}
#| eval: false

git update-git-for-windows

```



## Configure your credentials

Below you will need an account with *GitHub*, *GitLab* or *Bitbucket* (or similar). When asked to enter your `user.email`, use the one you have registered with a host server. Your `user.name` can be anything you feel comfortable with, but best is your actual name. 
If you don't want to sign up to a host server, you can use anything that looks like a valid email address. It will be stored in the metadata of the commits.

### via command line
Now you have to decide on an email-address and a name you want git to associate with you. We can do this via the command line (bash shell):

```{r}
#| eval: false
$ git config --global user.name "John Doe"
$ git config --global user.email johndoe@example.com
```

### in R via `usethis`
We can also do it in R via the `usethis` (or `devtools`) package
```{r}
#| eval: false

library(usethis) ## or library(devtools)
use_git_config(
  user.name = "Jane Doe", 
  user.email = "jane@example.com"
  )

# check by running a git situation-report:
# - your user.name and user.email should appear in global Git config
git_sitrep()


# to connect to GitHub you need a PAT (personal access token):
usethis::create_github_token()

# Now put your PAT into the git credentials store:
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()
```

### in Visual Studio Code

In VSC git can be used via the `Source Control` panel. To connect your repository to github, you need to:

1. open the command palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) and run *Publish to GitHub*
2. Sign in when prompted and return to VSC
3. Enter an available repository name and chose *private* or *public*
4. Make changes in your folder
5. stage (`add`) and `commit` them to the repository
6. `push` them to GitHub
